test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A dealer marked the price of an item 30% above the cost price. He allowed two successive discounts of 15% and 20% to a particular customer. As a result, he incurred a loss of ₹696. At what price did he sell the item to the customer?
solution:
**Given:**

Marked price (MP) = Cost price (CP) + 30% of CP

Discounts given: 15% and 20%

Loss incurred = ₹696

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (1 + 30/100)

Selling price (SP) after two successive discounts = MP × (1 - 15/100) × (1 - 20/100)

Loss = CP - SP

**Calculation:**

Let CP = ₹x

MP = x × (1 + 30/100)

⇒ MP = x × 1.3

SP after two successive discounts = MP × (1 - 15/100) × (1 - 20/100)

⇒ SP = x × 1.3 × 0.85 × 0.8

⇒ SP = x × 1.3 × 0.68

⇒ SP = x × 0.884

Loss = CP - SP

⇒ Loss = x - x × 0.884

⇒ ₹696 = x - x × 0.884

⇒ ₹696 = x(1 - 0.884)

⇒ ₹696 = x × 0.116

⇒ x = ₹696 / 0.116

⇒ x = ₹6,000

MP = ₹6,000 × 1.3

⇒ MP = ₹7,800

SP = ₹7,800 × 0.85 × 0.8

⇒ SP = ₹7,800 × 0.68

⇒ SP = ₹5,304

**The price at which the dealer sold the item is ₹5,304.**
